cases.name: Aminha Michelle Guy
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Aminah and her twin-sister Akasha, were born on January 26, 2005 in Santa Monica, California. Aminah has always exuded light and love, even as a young child. She just shined a bit brighter, a bit stronger, and at times, a bit louder than others, just ask Angie and Akasha. Lol. Aminah was very much the class line leader, student helper, peer leader, and teacher’s pet throughout elementary, middle, and high school.

All that Aminah wanted to do, she went after it relentlessly. All that she accomplished, she relished in it humbly. Aminah knew that her light was not accepted by everyone, it hurt her feelings from time to time, but it never deterred her. When faced with hardship, heartbreak, and an occasional hater, she pressed forward with hope.

Aminah was a planner, but more importantly she was a doer. She made color-coded lists, checked them twice, then shared her dreams and aspirations with trusted loved ones. Before moving forward, Aminah made time to pray. Even though she may not have vocalized it, Aminah’s faith in God was strong and she sought to grow in her personal relationship. Aminah attended World Overcomers Christian Church and visited First Cosmopolitan Baptist Church with Akasha, Audrina, Alana, and Ava.

Aminah’s light radiated through the halls of Athens Drive High School. She knew everyone and everyone knew her. In school, she did everything in excellence-student government association, basketball, track and field, and volleyball. She took honors courses and maintained honor roll status, only apart from the semester of covid. Lockdown and virtual learning were super tough on our shining star, but she kept her eyes set on going to college and playing volleyball. Aminah received many acceptance letters and scholarships, but she decided to continue in her family’s legacy of, Eagle Pride, Amplified-just like her Uncle Otis, Aunts Andrea, Courtney, and Nikki, and her sister-cousins Audrina and Alana. It made perfect sense as Aminah’s life was built on Truth & Service.

Aminah loved working with children. She was amazing with the littlest, whiniest, quietest, and busiest of them. She spent countless hours giving hugs and high-fives to her students at the Alexander Family YMCA in Raleigh. With studies, work, college volleyball, running for Miss Freshman, and beginning to attend sorority programs, Aminah continued to make time to visit her favorite little cousin Ava.

May the memories of Aminah’s bright smile, contagious joy, and tenacious spirit spur us all to plan, go, and do!"

cases.name: Rebecca Rene’ "Becky" Carter
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Rebecca graduated from Morristown High School in 2002. She worked at CubeSmart, for 18 years as a General Manager/Training Specialist. Rebecca trained many teammates and was a mentor and coach for the entire district. She won multiple All-Star awards for consistently going above and beyond, especially with her teammates.

Rebecca had a beautiful smile that would light up an entire room. She also had an infectious laugh. Rebecca was so full of life and a kid at heart. She loved to get together with friends and family. She enjoyed cooking and trying new recipes. Rebecca also loved to dance, sing and perform karaoke. Rebecca had a big heart and would go out of her way to help someone in need, especially her family."
cases.narrative: He told a detective that he strangled Carter and then stabbed her at least twice in the chest. He then allegedly left and brought a friend back to the apartment, where they consumed crack cocaine while Carter lay dead in the bedroom.
